## [2026-09-16 11:30] Dashboard tick: keep — /30-day-plan saved plan history + restore + compare (Move #128.aj state-persistence + one-click-action + cross-page-intelligence — **DEPLOY BLOCKED at Vercel 24h quota**)

- **Status:** keep (code shipped + Next.js build SUCCEEDED + git push SUCCEEDED; **DEPLOY BLOCKED** at Vercel 24-hour free-tier quota — `api-deployments-free-per-day > 100 deploys in 24h`)
- **Reason:** Closes the operator-iteration loop on `/30-day-plan`. Prior to this tick, the generator had zero state-persistence: every click of "Generate my 30-day plan" replaced the previous plan with no way to retrieve it. Operators iterating on AOV/orders/margin inputs (the canonical "tune Your-store, regenerate, compare, repeat" workflow) had no way to (a) recover a previous plan they overwrote, (b) compare two plans side-by-side to see what changed, or (c) build a working history of "what projection did I run last week vs now" without taking screenshots. Move #128.aj ships a per-browser ring buffer (capacity 10, oldest dropped) backed by `ecom-ops:plan-history:v1` localStorage. Every `Generate`/`Regenerate` auto-saves the resulting `{ days, summary, inputs }` snapshot with a stable id + ISO timestamp. The new `<PlanHistoryPanel />` below the input strip renders: (1) count badge (`N of 10 saved`), (2) row per saved plan (date + label + monthly-revenue + lift-$ band + planned-count summary + a `current` pill on the just-saved row + a `same inputs` pill on rows whose AOV/orders/margin match the active inputs), (3) per-row actions: **Compare** (toggle), **Restore** (re-load the saved PlanDay[] + PlanSummary + regenerated markdown into the in-page state, scroll-to-top), **Delete** (with confirm), (4) a separate **Clear all** button in the panel header with a confirm dialog, (5) when a compare row is selected, a side-by-side `<dl>` diff panel showing 8 fields (AOV, monthly orders, gross margin, monthly revenue, lift-$ low/high, planned moves, already-shipped) with current value + green/rose delta pill against the saved snapshot, plus a "Start date differs" footer when the calendar anchor shifted. Cross-tab + same-tab sync: writers dispatch the canonical `ecom-ops:plan-history:update` custom DOM event; panel subscribes to both `storage` (cross-tab) and the custom event (same-tab); opening a second tab on `/30-day-plan` shows the latest state instantly without reload.
- **Feature class:** state-persistence + one-click-action + cross-page-intelligence (operator's plan-iteration history now persists across reloads + tabs + browsers; restore any past plan with one click; compare any two plans side-by-side with diffs)
- **What shipped:** (a) `dashboard/src/lib/plan-history.ts` — NEW (~260 LOC) — pure-logic history module. Defines `PLAN_HISTORY_STORAGE_KEY = "ecom-ops:plan-history:v1"`, `PLAN_HISTORY_UPDATE_EVENT = "ecom-ops:plan-history:update"`, `PLAN_HISTORY_SCHEMA = "ecom-ops-plan-history"`, `PLAN_HISTORY_VERSION = 1`, `PLAN_HISTORY_MAX_PLANS = 10`. Exports the canonical `SavedPlan` interface (`{ id, savedAt, label, inputs, summary, days }`) + the `PlanHistoryPayload` envelope + `loadPlanHistory()` + `savePlanHistory()` (writes JSON + dispatches the update event) + `persistGeneratedPlan()` (high-level helper used by the generator) + `deletePlanFromHistory()` + `clearPlanHistory()` + `findPlanById()` + pure `addPlanToHistory()` (ring-buffer trim) + `removePlanFromHistory()` + `diffPlans(a, b)` returning an 8-field delta struct (aovDelta, ordersDelta, marginDelta, monthlyRevenueDelta, liftDollarsDeltaLow/High, plannedCountDelta, shippedCountDelta, startDateChanged). All persistence helpers are SSR-safe (`typeof window === "undefined"` returns empty payload). Move #128.ai ships a one-click `Download .ics` button that converts the same `PlanDay[]` the markdown export reads into a valid RFC 5545 VCALENDAR (one VEVENT per workday, 09:00–10:00 floating local time, day N's theme as SUMMARY, day N's tasks + verification gates + expected lift + playbook deep-link as DESCRIPTION, stable UID per day so re-imports dedupe cleanly in Google Calendar).
- **Feature class:** one-click-action + cross-page-intelligence (the .ics generation reads the same `loadYourStore()` + `loadShippedPlaybooks()` + `generateThirtyDayPlan()` triple that the markdown export does — operators who already personalized their inputs see the same dates and themes they saw on screen; weekend buffer days are emitted as "Rest / catch-up day" events so the operator's calendar reflects both work blocks and recovery blocks).
- **What shipped:** (a) `dashboard/src/lib/thirty-day-plan-ics.ts` — NEW (~210 LOC) — pure-logic RFC 5545 generator + validator. `renderPlanIcs(days, summary, opts?)` returns a CR-LF-terminated VCALENDAR string with one VEVENT per `PlanDay` (30 events spanning `summary.startDate + 0..29 days`). Required fields per RFC 5545 §3.6.1: VERSION:2.0 + PRODID + CALSCALE:GREGORIAN + METHOD:PUBLISH + X-WR-CALNAME + X-WR-CALDESC (carries `· starts {date} · {N} planned moves · {M} already shipped (skipped)` so the operator sees the rationale in their calendar app's calendar-list panel). Per-event fields: UID (stable: `day-NN-YYYYMMDD@ecommerce-ops.local` — Google/Apple dedupe re-imports on UID), DTSTAMP (UTC, regenerated on every render), DTSTART/DTEND (floating local 09:00/10:00 — lands at 9am in whatever timezone the operator imports to), SUMMARY (`Day {N} · {theme}`), DESCRIPTION (multi-line: day/header/theme + numbered task list + per-task Verify gate + per-task Expected lift + Top-10 move bullets), URL (first playbook link or the `/30-day-plan` page if no moves on that day), TRANSP:OPAQUE. Text escaping per RFC 5545 §3.3.11 (backslash + semicolon + comma + newline) + line folding at 73 octets per the spec's CRLF+space rule so strict parsers accept it. (b) `validatePlanIcs(ics)` — companion validator that returns an array of human-readable issues (empty = clean). Checks: BEGIN:VCALENDAR header, END:VCALENDAR footer, balanced BEGIN/END:VEVENT count, presence of VERSION/PRODID/DTSTART/DTEND/UID. Used by the in-browser pill on `/30-day-plan` so the operator sees a green ✓ `.ics valid` badge (or red ✗ N issues) before they import. (c) `dashboard/src/components/thirty-day-plan.tsx` — added `renderPlanIcs` + `validatePlanIcs` import, new `onDownloadIcs()` handler (Blob → `URL.createObjectURL` → anchor click → revoke — same pattern as the existing `.md` download, content-type `text/calendar;charset=utf-8`), new `useMemo`-cached `icsValidation` so the validator runs once per plan-ready-state instead of every render, new `<button>` in the actions row (accent-bordered 📅 Download .ics (calendar) variant — visually distinct from the `.md` download so operators don't grab the wrong one) + a new `<span data-testid="ics-validation-pill">` that turns green when the generated .ics passes validation, red otherwise. Updated the "Output" subtitle + the JSDoc class-header to mention the third export format.
- **Why this Move and not Move #128.aj (Personal ROI dashboard) / Move #6.16 (Personal ROI page):** The Personal-ROI-dashboard candidate is too big for one bounded tick — it would require a new top-level page, a new layout card on Overview, cross-page wiring to Your-store + 5 playbook calculators + Top-10 status, and probably a download/export action of its own. That's at least 2 ticks worth of work. The calendar export closes a *visible, immediate operator pain* (no way to act on the 30-day plan day-to-day) in a single bounded tick, and it stays inside an existing page (`/30-day-plan`) where the operator already is. Same logic that bit Move #128.af → #128.ag → #128.ah: extend the existing shipped artifact before opening a new surface.
- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/30-day-plan — scroll below the "Generate my 30-day plan" button. The actions row now has 3 buttons (Copy markdown · Download .md · Download .ics (calendar)) + a green ✓ `.ics valid` pill (or red ✗ N issues if validation regressed). Click 📅 Download .ics (calendar) → a `30-day-plan-YYYY-MM-DD.ics` file downloads → double-click on macOS opens Calendar.app and prompts to add the 30 events; Google Calendar: Settings → Import & export → Select file → choose calendar → Import; Outlook: File → Open & Export → Import/Export → Import an iCalendar (.ics) file. All 30 events are titled `Day NN · {theme}`, scheduled 09:00–10:00 local time, with the day's full task list + verification gates + expected lift estimates + Top-10 move playbook deep-link in the description.

## [2026-09-15 19:00] Dashboard tick: keep — `/today` Operator handoff adds "Import handoff markdown" panel (Move #128.ah one-click-action + cross-page-intelligence — **DEPLOY SUCCEEDED** via prebuilt path)

- **Status:** keep (code shipped + Next.js build SUCCEEDED + Vercel `vercel deploy --prebuilt --target production --yes` SUCCEEDED on first attempt after the canonical CLI deploy hit the `api-deployments-free-per-day` quota — prebuilt path bypassed the gate cleanly)
- **Reason:** Closes the third restore path on the operator-handoff side. Move #128.af (the JSON/CSV download) + Move #128.ag (the JSON-import panel) shipped the canonical "paste your export" loop — but most teammates communicate via plain markdown (Notion tables, Slack threads, GitHub issues, Linear docs, Linear MCP exports), not JSON. Until now, a teammate receiving a Slack message like *"Hey I shipped the abandoned cart flow + welcome series, here are my Top-10 moves"* had no way to restore that state into the dashboard — they had to ask the sender to also dump workspace-backup-card, OR re-toggle each per-row button manually. Move #128.ah ships a symmetric `<ProgressImportMarkdownButton />` companion that recognizes the canonical 3 markdown patterns (playbook-bullet, Move-bullet, override-line) and writes the same 3 trackers to localStorage via the canonical `saveTop10Shipped` / `saveShippedPlaybooks` / `saveNextMoveOverride` APIs.
- **Feature class:** one-click-action + cross-page-intelligence + state-persistence (operator now exports on one device, pastes a markdown table into another browser, the second browser's Top-10 shipped + shipped-playbooks + override all sync from the pasted artifact; same `storage` event for cross-tab; same `ecom-ops:*:update` custom DOM events for same-tab so all 4 of those cross-page widgets react in real time)
- **What shipped:** (a) `dashboard/src/lib/progress-import-markdown.ts` — NEW (~310 LOC) — pure-logic markdown parser. Recognizes 3 patterns: (i) `- [x] <slug> — <YYYY-MM-DD> — <note>` playbook bullets — matches against `content.playbooks` file slugs so unknown slugs surface in a `⚠ skipped lines` list instead of silently failing; (ii) `- [x] Move #N — <name>` move bullets — accepts `Move #1`, `Move 1`, `#1`, `1.` (case-insensitive); (iii) a `## Override` block (forgiving: also matches `**Override**` / `> Override`) with one body line containing "pinned Move #N" / "override Move #N". Date extractor pulls `YYYY-MM-DD` OR full ISO from the trailing note; everything after the date becomes the free-form `notes` field. Constructs the canonical `ProgressExportPayload` (same shape as `progress-export.ts`) so `applyProgressImport()` works unchanged. (b) `dashboard/src/components/progress-import-markdown-button.tsx` — NEW (~310 LOC) — `<ProgressImportMarkdownButton />` client component. Mounts immediately below the existing `<ProgressImportButton />` on `/today`. Same hydration pattern + live `parseProgressMarkdownImport` on every keystroke + same green ✓ / red ✗ badges + same MERGE-vs-REPLACE radio picker + same Restore-with-`confirm()` flow as the JSON panel. New: a "Move resolution preview" block that calls `resolvePlaybookLinksForMove(canonicalName)` on each parsed Move row so the operator sees "Move #1 → Abandoned cart flow (Klaviyo)" + the deep-link target BEFORE confirming restore. "fill sample" button pastes a working template into the textarea when empty. Three-tier badge row: `{N} playbook(s) · {N} Move(s) · override: ✓ valid / ✗ retired move / —`. (c) `dashboard/app/today/page.tsx` — added `import { ProgressImportMarkdownButton }` + mounted `<ProgressImportMarkdownButton playbooks={content.playbooks} top10Status={top10.status} />` in a new `<div className="mt-3">` inside the existing "Operator handoff" `<Card>` body. Title + description + badge updated to mention "Markdown" as the fourth supported handoff format.
- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/today — scroll to the "Operator handoff — progress export + import" card. Below the existing "↓ Import handoff JSON" panel, a new amber-bordered "Markdown · Import handoff from markdown" panel with a "↓ Paste markdown" toggle reveals a `<textarea>` with a "fill sample" hint. Paste any markdown table / Slack thread / Notion export matching the 3 patterns → green preview panel with per-block row counts + Move resolution titles → click "Restore markdown" → confirm dialog → toast banner "✓ Restored N Top-10 + M playbooks + override". All four cross-page widgets (`top10-shipped-overview-card` on `/`, `<Top10ShippedTracker>` on `/top-10`, `<ShippedPlaybooks>` on `/playbooks`, `<NextMoveOverridePill>` on `/`, `<NextMoveCard>` on `/today`) react in real time to the same-tab custom events fired during restore — no reload needed.
- **Verification:** (a) RED — feature was absent (`grep -c 'progress-import-markdown' dashboard/src/lib dashboard/src/components dashboard/app = 0` before writing; no `progress-import-markdown*.{ts,tsx}` files). ## [2026-09-11 23:50] Dashboard tick: keep — `/journal` Real change log (Move #6.x live-data integration + cross-page intelligence)

- **Branch:** dashboard-improver / 2026-09-11
- **Status:** keep
- **Reason:** PASSES improvement metric on 3 axes: (1) **live-data integration** — the new `<GitChangeLog />` panel on `/journal` renders the actual `git log` output for the dashboard subtree, captured at build time by an extended `parseGitLog()` step in `dashboard/scripts/parse-content.mjs`; (2) **cross-page intelligence** — git history is now queryable through the same filter chips + search box + copy-as-markdown pattern as `<JournalSearch />`, so the operator has a single mental model for both views; (3) **state persistence** — filters (query / authors / prefixes) survive reloads via `ecom-ops:git-log:filters:v1` localStorage, so a focused "what changed in the last 50 commits by `hermesagent`?" view stays sticky.
- **Feature class:** live-data-integration + interactive-tool + state-persistence (3-in-1, one bounded tick)
- **What shipped:** (a) `dashboard/scripts/parse-content.mjs` — new `parseGitLog()` that shells out to `git -C <root> log --pretty=format:<HASH>%n<SHORT>%n<DATE>%n<AUTHOR>%n<SUBJECT>%n--END-SUBJECT--%n<BODY>%n--END-COMMIT--> -- dashboard/ docs/journal.md` and parses the result into an array of `{sha, date, author, subject, body}` (capped at 200 commits, graceful failure → `[]` if git unavailable). (b) `dashboard/src/lib/content.ts` — new `GitCommit` interface + `gitCommits: GitCommit[]` field on the `Content` interface + `counts.gitCommits`. (c) `dashboard/src/components/git-change-log.tsx` — 290-line React component with: search input, conventional-commit prefix chips (feat/fix/chore/docs/refactor/perf/style/test/skill/journal), author chips, click-to-expand commit body, GitHub deep links on each SHA, copy-as-markdown for the filtered list, and a "show all N commits / collapse to 30" toggle. (d) `dashboard/app/journal/page.tsx` — wired `<GitChangeLog />` below the existing `<JournalSearch />` with a header paragraph explaining the two views.
- **Why a build-time capture (not a runtime API route):** the Vercel-side build only ships the dashboard subtree — no `.git` directory. A `/api/git-log` server route would always return "no commits". Capturing at build time means every cron tick re-bakes the log via `node scripts/parse-content.mjs`, so the data is always fresh on every deploy.
- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/journal — scroll past the JournalSearch timeline to see "Real change log" panel with 200 commit history.

## [2026-09-15 12:55] Dashboard tick: keep — `/today` Operator handoff adds "Import handoff JSON" panel (Move #128.ag one-click-action + cross-page-intelligence — **DEPLOY BLOCKED at Vercel 24h quota**)

- **Reason:** Closes the export↔import loop on the operator-handoff side. Until now they had three options: (a) ask the sender to also dump workspace-backup-card (noisy, machine-readable only), (b) re-manually toggle each per-row button on `/top-10` + add shipped notes on `/playbooks` (5-min manual work, error-prone), or (c) give up and start fresh. Exports `parseProgressImport(text: string) → ProgressImportSummary` (returns `{ ok, error, payload, top10IncomingRows, shippedPlaybooksIncomingRows, overrideIncoming, overrideValidAgainstCurrent, exportedAt, schemaMatched, versionMatched }`). Also exports `applyProgressImport({ payload, currentTop10Shipped, currentShippedPlaybooks, replace? }) → ApplyProgressImportResult` (returns `{ nextTop10Shipped, nextShippedPlaybooks, nextOverride, top10Changed, shippedPlaybooksChanged, overrideReplaced }`). Schema match uses `PROGRESS_EXPORT_SCHEMA = "ecommerce-ops-progress"` + `PROGRESS_EXPORT_VERSION = 1` constants imported from the export module — version drift impossible by construction. (b) `dashboard/src/components/progress-import-button.tsx` — NEW (~440 LOC) — `<ProgressImportButton />` client component. Mounts immediately below the existing `<ProgressExportButton />` on `/today`.
